question:
In a manufacturing facility, you are tasked with scheduling the production of two distinct jobs, Job 0 and Job 1, across a set of machines. Each job consists of a sequence of operations that must be performed in a specific order, and each operation requires a certain amount of time to complete. The goal is to minimize the total production time, known as the makespan, while ensuring that all operations are scheduled without overlapping on the same machine and that the sequence of operations within each job is respected.

Job 0 consists of two operations: Operation 0 takes 5 units of time to complete, and Operation 1 can only start after Operation 0 has finished. The makespan must be at least 5 units of time after the start of Operation 0 and at least 2 units of time after the start of Operation 1.

Job 1 consists of five operations: Operation 0 takes 9 units of time to complete, Operation 1 takes 9 units of time and can only start after Operation 0 has finished, Operation 2 takes 7 units of time and can only start after Operation 1 has finished, Operation 3 takes 2 units of time and can only start after Operation 2 has finished, and Operation 4 takes 8 units of time and can only start after Operation 3 has finished. The makespan must be at least 9 units of time after the start of Operation 0, at least 9 units of time after the start of Operation 1, at least 7 units of time after the start of Operation 2, at least 2 units of time after the start of Operation 3, and at least 8 units of time after the start of Operation 4.

Certain operations from Job 1 must be performed on the same machine, and their scheduling must avoid overlaps. Specifically, Operation 0 and Operation 4 of Job 1 cannot overlap on the same machine. If Operation 0 starts first, Operation 4 must start at least 8 units of time after Operation 0 finishes. Conversely, if Operation 4 starts first, Operation 0 must start at least 9 units of time after Operation 4 finishes. Similarly, Operation 2 and Operation 3 of Job 1 cannot overlap on the same machine. If Operation 2 starts first, Operation 3 must start at least 2 units of time after Operation 2 finishes. Conversely, if Operation 3 starts first, Operation 2 must start at least 7 units of time after Operation 3 finishes.

The primary objective is to minimize the makespan, which is the total time taken to complete all operations across both jobs. The makespan must be at least as long as the completion time of the last operation in either job. All operations must start at or after time 0, and the order of operations within each job must be strictly followed. The scheduling of operations on shared machines must respect the no-overlap constraints described above. Binary variables are used to enforce the no-overlap constraints on the shared machines, ensuring that the operations do not overlap and the sequence constraints are satisfied.

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# =============================================================================
# DATA: every numeric constant from the problem statement
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# proc[j][o] : processing time of operation o of job j
# precedence : (job, predecessor op, successor op) within-job ordering
# machine_pairs : (job_a, op_a, job_b, op_b) sharing a machine (disjunctive)
#   For pair (a, b):
#     if a precedes b : s_b >= s_a + p_a
#     if b precedes a : s_a >= s_b + p_b
# bigM : sufficiently large constant to deactivate a disjunctive constraint
# =============================================================================
DATA = {
    "proc": {
        0: [5, 2],
        1: [9, 9, 7, 2, 8],
    },
    "precedence": [
        (0, 0, 1),
        (1, 0, 1),
        (1, 1, 2),
        (1, 2, 3),
        (1, 3, 4),
    ],
    # Job 1 op0 & op4 share a machine; Job 1 op2 & op3 share a machine.
    "machine_pairs": [
        (1, 0, 1, 4),
        (1, 2, 1, 3),
    ],
    "bigM": 1000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Sets
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=list(d["proc"].keys()), ordered=True)

    ops_index = [(j, o) for j in d["proc"] for o in range(len(d["proc"][j]))]
    model.OPS = pyo.Set(initialize=ops_index, dimen=2, ordered=True)

    model.PREC = pyo.Set(initialize=d["precedence"], dimen=3, ordered=True)

    model.MPAIR = pyo.Set(initialize=d["machine_pairs"], dimen=4, ordered=True)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Variables
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    model.s = pyo.Var(model.OPS, domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.Cmax = pyo.Var(domain=pyo.NonNegativeReals)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.MPAIR, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # Objective: minimize makespan
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (1) Precedence within each job
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def prec_rule(m, j, o1, o2):
        return m.s[j, o2] >= m.s[j, o1] + d["proc"][j][o1]

    model.precedence_con = pyo.Constraint(model.PREC, rule=prec_rule)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (2) Makespan lower bounds: Cmax >= s[j,o] + p[j,o]
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def makespan_rule(m, j, o):
        return m.Cmax >= m.s[j, o] + d["proc"][j][o]

    model.makespan_con = pyo.Constraint(model.OPS, rule=makespan_rule)

    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # (3) Disjunctive no-overlap on shared machines
    #     y = 1 -> a before b ; y = 0 -> b before a
    # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    M = d["bigM"]

    def disj_a_rule(m, ja, oa, jb, ob):
        return m.s[jb, ob] >= m.s[ja, oa] + d["proc"][ja][oa] - M * (1 - m.y[ja, oa, jb, ob])

    def disj_b_rule(m, ja, oa, jb, ob):
        return m.s[ja, oa] >= m.s[jb, ob] + d["proc"][jb][ob] - M * m.y[ja, oa, jb, ob]

    model.disj_a_con = pyo.Constraint(model.MPAIR, rule=disj_a_rule)
    model.disj_b_con = pyo.Constraint(model.MPAIR, rule=disj_b_rule)

    return model

# =============================================================================
# Problem analysis / verification of checks
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# (1) Big-M parametrisation: The text gives each disjunctive pair its own
#     offset ("at least 8 units after Operation 0 finishes", "at least 9
#     ... after Operation 4 finishes"). A redundant single global big-M = 1000
#     grouped all constraints. It is preferable to compute per-pair M from
#     DATA so that no magic numbers appear in the model. Text supports it.
#
# (2) Which operation precedes which in each disjunctive pair: One representative
#     encodes this with a single binary y (y=1 -> a before b). That is a
#     faithful linearisation of the "if ... first ... conversely ..." text.
#
# (3) Makespan lower bounds per operation: correctly listed.
#
# (4) "All operations start at or after 0": modelled via NonNegativeReals.
#
# =============================================================================

DATA = {
    # Processing times per job (indexed by job -> list of ops in order)
    "proc": {
        0: [5, 2],
        1: [9, 9, 7, 2, 8],
    },
    # Precedence pairs (job, predecessor op, successor op)
    "precedence": [
        (0, 0, 1),
        (1, 0, 1),
        (1, 1, 2),
        (1, 2, 3),
        (1, 3, 4),
    ],
    # Disjunctive machine pairs: (job_a, op_a, job_b, op_b)
    # y = 1 -> a precedes b, offset on b is p_a
    # y = 0 -> b precedes a, offset on a is p_b
    "machine_pairs": [
        (1, 0, 1, 4),
        (1, 2, 1, 3),
    ],
    # Safety big-M margin: the per-pair M is sum of remaining processing times
    # plus this horizon safeguard, computed below (no hardcoded 1000).
    "horizon_pad": 0,
}

# Derived: give big-M per pair from summed processing times.
def _pair_big_M(d, ja, oa, jb, ob):
    total = sum(sum(lst) for lst in d["proc"].values())
    return total + d["horizon_pad"]


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    # ---------------- Sets ----------------
    model.J = pyo.Set(initialize=list(d["proc"].keys()), ordered=True)
    ops_index = [(j, o) for j in d["proc"] for o in range(len(d["proc"][j]))]

    model.y = pyo.Var(model.MPAIR, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # ---------------- Objective ----------------
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(expr=model.Cmax, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # ---------------- Precedence within a job ----------------
    def prec_rule(m, j, o1, o2):
        return m.s[j, o2] >= m.s[j, o1] + d["proc"][j][o1]

    model.precedence_con = pyo.Constraint(model.PREC, rule=prec_rule)

    # ---------------- Makespan lower bounds ----------------
    def makespan_rule(m, j, o):
        return m.Cmax >= m.s[j, o] + d["proc"][j][o]

    model.makespan_con = pyo.Constraint(model.OPS, rule=makespan_rule)

    # ---------------- Disjunctive no-overlap ----------------
    # y[pair] = 1 -> a before b
    # y[pair] = 0 -> b before a
    def disj_a_rule(m, ja, oa, jb, ob):
        M = _pair_big_M(d, ja, oa, jb, ob)
        return m.s[jb, ob] >= m.s[ja, oa] + d["proc"][ja][oa] - M * (1 - m.y[ja, oa, jb, ob])

    def disj_b_rule(m, ja, oa, jb, ob):

        return m.s[ja, oa] >= m.s[jb, ob] + d["proc"][jb][ob] - M * m.y[ja, oa, jb, ob]

    model.disj_a_con = pyo.Constraint(model.MPAIR, rule=disj_a_rule)
